title: f.e.a.r.
text: Fear was the system hog of its time. It was also touted as one of the best FPS titles of its time. Does it hold up to both those titles today. Well, yes and no. Yes it's one of the best FPS titles of its time (and still an impressive shooter nowadays), no it's no longer a system hog. Let's look deeper into that. FEAR puts you in control of Point Man, the newest member of a government team meant to combat paranormal threats. You're sent out to stop a crazed cannibalistic solider who's taken telepathic command of an army of clone soldiers. Meanwhile, there's this creepy girl stalking you through the whole thing and making people explode into meat splatters with her telepathic abilities. The whole game is pretty much you tracking down the cannibal freak, killing clone soldiers, investigating the situation's backstory, and discovering all the dirty little secrets. It's a mildly intriguing story, but i'll admit it's never really hooked me. The gameplay on the other hand... Woo boy. This game has some of the best shooting i've ever come across, even by today's standards. If you've ever watched a John Woo film, you know what you're gonna get here. the gunfights here are cinematic, frenetic, fast-paced encounters where bullets tear chunks out of concrete, glass windows are shattered, bodies fly around like ragdolls, blood splatters, smoke emanates from gun barrels, dust clouds your vision, and furniture is obliterated. Despite the near complete lack of enemy variety (they're all literally clones), the action never gets old. All this is made even better by the smart enemy AI. Clones pin you down, shout orders to their squad mates, flank you while the others keep you in cover with gunfire, throw grenades your way, jump over ledges to avoid your bullets, run away from your grenades, take defensive positions, crawl under tables for cover, notice your flashlight, and even hear your footsteps if you don't crouch. The AI here was ahead of its time and still impresses today. The game's also pretty scary and atmospheric too. I wouldn't call it terrifyin, but I will say it managed to give me the chills and jolt me many, many times. Disturbing hallucinations, that creepy ghost girl stalking you, chilling music, and things moving on their own all work together to unsettle you whenever you're not locked in a fierce firefight with enemies. Like I said though, the graphics have already been eclipsed tons of times in the years following this game's release. It simply isn't all that demanding anymore. On a mid-range laptop, you can easily run it at max settings with 60 frames per seconds. The visuals themselves are very sharp at max settings, but not exactly impressive. Textures are... all right. Water effects are fairly basic. The two places the graphics are still fairly impressive are in the lighting effects and, especially, the particles. Remember what I said about how the environments just come apart when you're in gunfights? Yeah, the particle effects actually add to the gameplay here and turning them down deals a serious blow to the enjoyment in my opinion. Overall: recommended. It's a solid, exciting shooter worth your time and money. Not for the graphics enthusiasts (though the game isn't what you'd call ugly), but definitely for shooter fans and anyone who wants to see some terrific AI at work. Pros: Frenetic, intense, satisying combat Impressively smart AI Great music and sound effects Genuinely chilling Not hard to run nowadays Cons: Visuals aren't all that impressive anymore

title: f.e.a.r. 2: project origin
text: F.E.A.R 2: Project Origin is made by same development studio, Monolith Productions but had different publisher, which is WB Interactive Entertainment. The game has a different protagonist, Michael Becket, who gains fast reflexes after being captured and recovered at the hospital. From this point, you try to find out why Alma takes interest at you, what is your history with Armacham Technology Corporation and what to do next. First F.E.A.R is known for slow-mo ability, smart A.I and great gunplay. Does F.E.A.R 2: Project Origin offer the same experience or is it better or worse? Worse. + You can aim with iron sights now. This allows you to use sniper rifles, which is a great addition. + There are two mech-suit sections, which honestly are fun. Might be off-putting to some players, but I personally liked those sections. Offered something different for gameplay. + This game doesn't take your weapons away at any moment, so you can spare your equipment for difficult encounters. + Slow-mo: It still looks cool to kill enemies when time is slowed down. It's mandatory to use it in order to survive, which is fine in my opinion. + Scary factor: While some of these are predictable (No scares when human enemies are near), most of the time they might spook you. + You can now cook off granades. * Graphics look better, but the style and lighting is much more bland, especially the lighting. Compare it to previous game and say which looks better. * A bit more open areas than in first game, but they limit them with invisible walls and fences, which you could clearly overstep. * Some in-game awards if you want be completionist, but they could've been steam achievements (Old game, so it's not in cons). - A.I: I don't know why people say that A.I is better because in my experience, enemies are much more dumber than in first F.E.A.R. They manage to kill themselves with their own granades and seem to rush to player more often. There is also less interaction between enemy soldiers. What I liked about previous game is that enemies react to what you're doing. There wasn't much, but it was something and you could actually use their talk as your advantage. In F.E.A.R 2 only thing that I remember is them saying "He's too fast". A.I wasn't perfect in F.E.A.R but it was much more advanced than an average one, which could've been improved upon. Very dissapointing. -Saves: Monolith Productions took off manual saves and quick saves and replaced them with auto-saves/checkpoints. I don't understand why they did this. Most checkpoints work fine, but some of them are plain horrible. For example, I finished off one turret section, decided to take some ammunition from dead replicas, noticed a rocket launcher. Then I checked its ammunation by replacing it with a weapon given by that one guy, and it disappeared. I wanted it back so I loaded a previous checkpoint, which WAS BEFORE THE TURRET SECTION! - Story: This is a subjective thing and my opinion is that it isn't good. Most of the characters weren't interesting, except for . Ending was pretty anti-climatic in my opinion. - You cannot lean on to anything anymore. Why was leaning removed? - Some gameplay elements: Melee strikes are still awful. In my playthrough, there were so many weird misses that led to my death. Now, playing on hard difficulty, the game is suppose to be challenging. It does that, but there are so many ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t moments. Sometimes it requires you to shoot enemies with shotgun like four times, but they can hit you from same distance only once and kill you. - Hearing distance: Sometimes there is barely any audio cues when someone is approaching you. Usually that happens when they come from behind. If don't put your audio to maximum, you usually miss them and then enemy manages to kill you with easily. Sneaking type enemies almost always require slow-mo, which in of itself isn't bad but I wish there were more indications. That one tram sequence: I hated it. Audio glitched off, so I couldn't hear where enemies come from and that includes their weapons. This resulted in many unfair deaths. F.E.A.R 2: Project Origin is plain average game. There are too many things removed and new additions aren't enough. For me, it's 4/10 or 5/10. Like always, if there was something I missed, any possible mistakes or something that you thought was worth noting, please let me know in the comments. Otherwise, if you liked F.E.A.R, you probably like F.E.A.R 2 due to bullet-time and scares, but if you are a hardcore fan of the first game, you most likely dislike this one.

title: f.e.a.r. 2: project origin
text: Awful port to an okay game. This game pales in comparison to the first game. The enemy AI doesn't feel as smart and makes the game a lot easier, and the hit markers make it feel like a modern cliche military shooter. Even with the sensitivity slider all the way down and with the lowest dpi settings, the sensitivity in the game stills feels high, and I experienced a huge drop in framerate at the start of the last interval. I managed to make it somewhat playable by lowering the resolution, but the fps still dropped below 20 at some points. I am very disappointed with this game.

title: f.e.a.r. 2: project origin
text: A remarkable game, sure it won't scare you in the same way the first game did, but it is a class A shooter with improved graphics, impvored cover and AI. The story will keep you on the edge of your chair just as much as the action. If you loved FEAR's multiplayer aspect this offers more in the way of options and remains just as fun.
